subject.title: feat: allow global pairing reply templates

question: Should OpenClaw support `messages.pairingTemplate` as a permanent global configuration contract, and if so should customized templates be required to include `{code}` or `{approveCommand}`?
rationale: The repository intentionally keeps config and Plugin SDK surfaces small; accepting arbitrary templates and public override parameters establishes product and compatibility policy that cannot be inferred safely from implementation alone.

options.title: Approve a narrowed global template
options.body: Add the global setting, require an actionable approval placeholder, and keep resolver/per-call override parameters out of the public Plugin SDK.

options.title: Approve fully flexible templates
options.body: Explicitly accept empty or non-actionable templates and document the new public Plugin SDK override behavior as supported contract.

options.title: Decline the new config surface
options.body: Keep the built-in shared pairing reply and use code-level plugin customization only where channel owners require different behavior.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrowed global template
recommendation.body: Add the global setting, require an actionable approval placeholder, and keep resolver/per-call override parameters out of the public Plugin SDK.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent Plugin SDK and shared-channel work is closest to both the product boundary and the public API decision.
